question: is the rejected S16-V checkpoint on the Hub so a third party can audit the 16 GB NO, does every published byte match the digests receipts/sixteen-flip-kld.json recorded from the local tree before the upload, and was the local copy released only after that was proven?
policy: docs/29 'Preservation: preserve before delete'. Upload first, re-verify the remote copy against the local bytes, and only then treat the local copy as expendable. tools/preserve_artifacts.sh never deletes: it prints the delete command and a human (here, this agent, after reading the verification output) runs it.
why_a_rejected_build_is_published_at_all: the measurement receipt's pre-registered rule sent a clear NO to deletion, and its own recommendation to the owner was to override that and upload anyway on the EDA precedent: it is the only sub-4-bit artifact in this family, it is the empirical anchor for the K3 rung of docs/37's per-bit law, and a NO nobody can audit is an assertion rather than a result. This receipt records the override being taken.

model_repo.naming: malaiwah/Qwen3.8-27B-EXL3-<recipe>-research, the suffix this family already uses for a published negative (malaiwah/Qwen3.8-27B-EXL3-EDA-research). The recipe name S16-V is docs/34 6.1's.

model_repo.why_preserved: the auditable copy of a rejected build: 0.045374 mean KLD [0.041959, 0.049351] on v5 shard 0, 1.5x the pre-registered NO threshold, losing 512 of 512 contexts to K4 and 512 of 512 to the context edition. It is also the only sub-4-bit artifact in this family, so it carries the 336 realised K3 modules that test the 3.73x-per-bit law one rung below where it was fitted.
model_repo.recompute_cost: receipts/sixteen-flip-kld.json records roughly 41 minutes of GPU for the conversion; the successful attempt's own step logs span 16:18:21Z to 16:57:04Z, about 39 minutes (the first attempt, at 16:10:56Z, died in the checkpoint save under proot). Plus ~6 min to capture 512 contexts and ~3 to replay. A fresh conversion returns a sibling and not these bytes.

what_verification_means_here.remote-sha256-lfs-oid: the Hub's own LFS object id is a sha256 over the stored content, compared against the local sha256. End-to-end on the full bytes without re-downloading them.
what_verification_means_here.remote-git-blob-id: sha1 over 'blob <len>\0' + content, for files the Hub does not put in LFS.
what_verification_means_here.served-sha256-readback: the file was re-downloaded from the CDN and re-hashed: a claim about what the Hub actually serves, not only about metadata it computed.
what_verification_means_here.served-sha256-readback-lfs-spot: the same, for LFS files. Both uploads ran with --spot all, so this covers EVERY LFS file rather than a sample: 4 of 4 safetensors-class files for K6-parity and 3 of 3 for S16-V. Nothing in either tree was released on metadata alone.
what_verification_means_here.digests_vs_build_receipt: each verified digest was additionally compared against build.tree of the measurement receipt, which was written from the local tree before anything was uploaded. The upload is checked against the record, not against itself.
what_verification_means_here.problems: any missing file, size disagreement or digest disagreement exits non-zero and prints no delete command. Both uploads reported an empty problem list.
